title: [AlwaysOnTop] Excluded apps should be able to use the registered keboard shortcut
author: rp1231

status.label: Not a bug-fix candidate
status.detail: This is a feature request that changes global shortcut routing semantics, not a defect with an isolated PowerToys fix.

next_action.label: Clarify excluded-app hotkey behavior
next_action.reason: Reclassify as an enhancement/product-direction request and recommend a non-conflicting Always On Top shortcut unless per-app pass-through is approved.

judgment.rationale: This is a feature request that changes global shortcut routing semantics, not a defect with an isolated PowerToys fix.
evidence: The body explicitly describes a new-feature scenario.
The same Alt+Z chord is intentionally assigned to two consumers.
judgment.recommended_action: Reclassify as an enhancement/product-direction request and recommend a non-conflicting Always On Top shortcut unless per-app pass-through is approved.

fix_assessment.rationale: A bug fix is not applicable because current exclusion behavior is consistent; conditional hotkey pass-through is a separately scoped enhancement.

issue_context.summary: An app excluded from Always On Top still cannot use the same activation chord because the chord is registered globally even though the module declines to pin the excluded window.
known_information: The report is written as a feature/enhancement scenario despite carrying an Issue-Bug label.
The desired Alt+Z chord is used both by Blender and as the user's Always On Top shortcut.
Always On Top exclusion controls whether ProcessCommand acts on a window, not whether the centralized/global hotkey listener reserves the chord.
inferences: Passing the same chord through only for selected foreground apps requires a different hook-routing/product design, not a local exclusion bug fix.
issue_context.analysis: The current behavior follows the architecture: exclusion prevents pinning, while hotkey registration/listening remains global. The actionable decision is product direction—use a non-conflicting shortcut today or separately approve per-app hotkey pass-through semantics.
initial_investigation: AlwaysOnTop::ProcessCommand returns when the foreground window is excluded.
Hotkey registration/listening is configured independently of the excluded-app check.
No implementation pull request references issue 27189.

actions.label: Clarify excluded-app hotkey behavior
actions.note: Draft only; no upstream comment is posted without explicit approval.

comment.body: The excluded-app list prevents Always On Top from changing the matching window, but the activation shortcut is still a global PowerToys shortcut. Allowing Blender to receive the same Alt+Z chord only while it is foreground would require new per-app hotkey pass-through semantics rather than a correction to exclusion matching. For current behavior, please choose a non-conflicting Always On Top shortcut. This issue should be tracked as an enhancement/product-direction request if conditional pass-through is desired.
